name: Line, obstacle, laser and motion sensors
author: Bench Workshop
description: Sensors robots use: the TCRT5000 line sensor (sees dark lines on a light floor), the FC-51 obstacle sensor (IR, a few cm), the VL53L0X laser distance sensor (I2C, up to 2 m) and the HC-SR501 PIR motion sensor. They really look at the bench. Includes VL53L0X.h and Adafruit_VL53L0X.h.

parts.name: Line sensor (TCRT5000)
parts.description: Looks straight down (put it 0.5-2 cm above the floor, under a robot): DO is LOW over a light surface and HIGH over a dark line; AO gives more volts the darker it is. VCC (3.3-5 V), GND. Lines: dark plates or blocks on a light one.

parts.name: Obstacle sensor (FC-51)
parts.description: An IR LED and a receiver looking forward (along +x, the way its LEDs point): OUT goes LOW when something is closer than its range (2-30 cm, its knob), HIGH otherwise. VCC (3.3-5 V), GND.

parts.name: Laser distance sensor (VL53L0X)
parts.description: Measures how far the first thing ahead is (along +x), 3 cm to 2 m, in millimetres, over I2C (address 0x29). VIN (3.3-5 V), GND, SCL, SDA. With VL53L0X.h: sensor.init(); sensor.startContinuous(); sensor.readRangeContinuousMillimeters(). 8190 = nothing in range.

parts.name: Motion sensor (HC-SR501 PIR)
parts.description: Sees things move in front of it (along +x, a wide cone, a few metres): OUT goes high (3.3 V) for its hold time after it sees movement. VCC (5-12 V), GND. It needs a couple of seconds to settle when it gets power.

examples.name: How far? (VL53L0X)
examples.description: A laser distance sensor looking at a block: the distance in the serial monitor. Drag the block while it runs.

examples.name: Obstacle and line
examples.description: An obstacle sensor and a line sensor lighting LEDs: the line sensor sits over a black strip on white, the obstacle sensor looks at a block. Drag things while it runs.
